shortcut_name: product-two constraints reduce directly to bipartite coloring
evidence: deepseek: "color[start] = 0" and "color[v] = 1 - color[u]"; gpt-oss: uses component coloring and orientation; qwen3-coder: "This is essentially checking bipartiteness"; glm-5: maintains a graph color and propagates colors across edges
affordance_in_statement: every projector must be assigned a pulse cycle of either 1 or 2 microseconds ... the mathematical product of their assigned pulse cycles must equal exactly 2
removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving wording change that removes this reduction: with values restricted to 1 and 2, product exactly 2 intrinsically means that every connected edge joins opposite values. Removing the affordance requires changing the edge constraint itself, not merely rephrasing it.

common_affordance: The domain {1, 2} together with the edge condition that the endpoint product equals 2 makes every edge require unequal endpoint values, reducing the task to bipartite graph coloring.
recommended_edit: No semantics-preserving edit can defeat all survivors because this is the intrinsic structure of the stated constraints. To defeat the shortcut, replace the edge relation with a genuinely different or additional constraint whose valid endpoint assignments are not exactly the unequal pairs; this necessarily changes the underlying task.
